titre: James Webb discovery of JADES-GS-z14-0, the galaxy that shouldn't exist
resume: The James Webb Space Telescope found JADES-GS-z14-0, a galaxy at redshift about 14.18 formed roughly 300 million years after the Big Bang, over 1,600 light years wide with millions of stars. Spectroscopy showed ionized oxygen, a heavy element that requires generations of stars, contradicting Cold Dark Matter predictions.
texte: This isn’t just the random ramblings of theoretical physicists searching for some alternative explanation to the Big Bang. It’s a framework that’s based on actual data captured at the edge of observable space. That’s where the James Webb Space Telescope, or JWST comes in. Its Near-Infrared Camera and Mid-Infrared Instrument scoured deep space and locked onto a galaxy named JADES-GS-z14-0. This galaxy has a red-shift of about 14.18, which means that it’s one of the most distant galaxies ever discovered. The galaxy formed around 13.5 billion years ago, or around 300 million years after the Big Bang. According to the Lambda Cold Dark Matter framework, space at that time should have been empty, aside from primordial gas clouds swirling around dark matter pockets. It certainly shouldn’t have contained any complex, fully-formed galaxies. JADES-GS-z14-0 measures up at more than 1,600 light years wide and is packed with millions of stars. But the real smoking gun was the spectroscopic analysis, which found signatures of heavy elements, including ionized oxygen. This goes against the Cold Dark Matter model. That says that hydrogen and helium might be present around the time this galaxy formed. But oxygen can only appear after generations of stars being born, fusing, dying. It’s the galaxy that shouldn’t exist. And that’s just the start.
